relevance_note: First-hand report of two infants with TNFAIP3 variants: "Herein, we report two children with the primary presentation of HLH, with a mutation in TNFAIP3, in favor of HA20."
method_note: Read the whole paper by hand; a Python script assembled the JSON from values I transcribed, and I checked every span verbatim by script. Scope: the two first-hand patients (headings 'Patient one' and 'Patient two'; Table 3 rows 3 and 4 'Our patient N. 1/2', same people), the two tested-negative parents of Patient two, two previously published patients in Table 3 (rows 1 'Li at el', ref [29], and 2 'Takagi et al', ref [9]; each also described in the Discussion text and treated as the same person as its table row), and three patients of Zhang et al. 2021 [25] described with individual features in the Discussion. Their HA20 status is implied by the paragraph on HA20 patients, not stated per patient; no variant is printed for them, so they have no variant rows. Left out: the healthy, untested older sister of Patient one and the untested consanguineous parents of Patient one (neither tested nor affected); Zhou et al. and other references without individual-level facts. Table 3 has a bare 'Number' column, hence labels 'Table 3 #1' and 'Table 3 #2' for the literature patients. Table 3 'Other features' is '-' for our patients; the legend does not define '-', so nothing was excluded from it. Li patient variant: text gives 'c.259C > T (p.R87X)' with 'RS: NM_006290'; Table 3 gives 'c.C259T, p.R87X'; recorded the text form. Takagi patient: text says 'de novo mutation of TNFAIP3 was detected' without stating parental testing, so inheritance is 'not reported' (rule 8). Patient one: zygosity and inheritance are not stated; parental testing not described. Patient two: SIFT/PolyPhen-2 'probably deleterious' and CADD 29.1 are in-silico predictions, not recorded as authors' classification or functional evidence. Checklist: 'recurrent fever' marked observed only for 'intermittent fever'; single or prolonged fever episodes (Patient two, Table 3 #1, #2) left 'not reported'. Cytopenias from HLH were not counted as 'cytopenia (autoimmune)'. Patient one cerebral hemorrhage counted as central nervous system involvement. Group statements naming 'our patients'/'Both of our patients' (no autoantibodies; no Behcet-like or autoimmune symptoms; MAS criteria) were applied to both patients as 'inferred from group statement'; the Behcet-like/autoimmune statement was not mapped to specific checklist items. Normal findings recorded per D-27 (ESR, CRP, procalcitonin, FANA, PT, lymphocyte subsets, NBT, immunoglobulins, CSF, cultures). General normal findings not converted to features: urine analysis and stool exam, echocardiography, vital signs, metabolic evaluation, serology, BCG scar and tonsils, 'No other abnormality was found'. Patient two coagulation profile 'normal, except for thrombocytopenia' sits beside fibrinogen 93* (hypofibrinogenemia); no coagulation-profile row was emitted. Contradictions in the paper: (1) Patient one text says 'normal ESR, CRP' but Table 1 gives ESR 11 with range 0-10 (CRP 6 vs <6); recorded as excluded from the text. (2) Patient two: 'proline to leucine amino acid change (p. L275P)' while the notation reads leucine to proline. (3) Background says 'we present a case' though the paper reports two cases. Patient two age at genetic diagnosis and age at last evaluation are not stated ('4 years have passed since the first presentation'). No stacked (' / ') cells in this paper.
